opportunities.name: GitHub developer lead research → hiring email
opportunities.description: For a given GitHub username and job role, find the user on GitHub, open their profile and top repo, collect followers/stars/language/latest blog post, then draft a lead email to hiring@example.com.
steps: On GitHub, open 'Search or jump to' and type the {username}, press Enter
Filter results to 'Users' and open the {username} profile
Note follower count and open the top/pinned repository; note its stars and language
Check the user's latest blog post title
In mail, compose a new message To: hiring@example.com
Body: '{username}: {followers} followers, top repo {repo} ({stars} stars, {language}), latest post: {latest_post}.'
Send (in the recording, the draft was discarded)

instances.values: karpathy; role ML Research Engineer; repo nanoGPT (63.8k stars, Python); 226k followers (a weather search interrupted this one)
gaearon; role Staff Frontend Engineer; repo react/react (251.1k stars, JavaScript); 94k followers
simonw; role Developer Advocate; repo llm (12.6k stars, Python); 17.3k followers (a Chicago Loop lookup interrupted this one)

opportunities.name: Person bio + Wayback Machine homepage snapshot → note
opportunities.description: For a given person, organisation domain and year, look up the person's birth date and role on Wikipedia, open the domain's archived homepage from that year on the Wayback Machine, read the headline, and save a combined note.
steps: On Wikipedia, search for {person} and open the article
Note the birth date and current/main role
On the Wayback Machine, enter {domain} and press Enter
Pick year {year} in the timeline and open a snapshot day in the calendar
Read the main headline on the archived homepage
In notes, add a new note: '{person}: born {birth_date}, {role}. {domain} in {year}: {headline}'

opportunities.name: Address → nearest park (OpenStreetMap) + neighbourhood summary note
opportunities.description: For a given street address, find the nearest park and the walking distance/time on OpenStreetMap, look up the neighbourhood on Wikipedia, and save a note.
steps: On OpenStreetMap, search for {address} and find the nearest park
Get walking directions to note the distance and walking time
On Wikipedia, search for {neighborhood} and read the summary
In notes, add: '{address}: nearest park {park}, distance {distance}, walking time {time}. {neighborhood}: {summary}'

instances.values: 233 S Wacker Dr, Chicago; Chicago Loop. OpenStreetMap returned HTTP 429, so the note says the park details are unavailable. There were also failed OpenStreetMap reloads at t=450.8 and t=550.7, but no note was saved for those.
